extracted.intended_audience: State agencies, health insurance issuers, Exchanges, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and other stakeholders affected by ACA Exchange and premium stabilization program rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and program requirements governing Exchanges, QHP certification, premium stabilization programs (risk adjustment/risk corridors/reinsurance), program integrity, and Essential Health Benefits under the Affordable Care Act and related legislation. Includes statutory directives and finalized regulatory parameters from prior Payment Notices and Federal Register rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to cover Essential Health Benefits (EHB)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1301(a)(1)(B) directs all issuers of qualified health plans (QHPs) to cover the Essential Health Benefit (EHB) package described in section 1302(a) of the Affordable Care Act, including coverage of the services described in section 1302(b), adherence to the cost-sharing limits in section 1302(c), and meeting the Actuarial Value (AV) levels in section 1302(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a QHP certification criterion; EHB coverage, cost-sharing limits, and AV levels are core components for plan qualification as a QHP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of EHB requirement to non-grandfathered coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2707(a) of the PHS Act extends the requirement to cover the EHB package to non-grandfathered individual and small group health insurance coverage, irrespective of whether such coverage is offered through an Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-grandfathered plans must provide EHB-equivalent coverage even if sold off-exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-sharing limits for non-grandfathered group health plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2707(b) directs non-grandfathered group health plans to ensure that cost sharing under the plan does not exceed the limitations described in section 1302(c)(1) of the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan design must reflect statutory cost-sharing caps; compliance affects plan permissibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: EHB scope and ten categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1302 requires that EHB be equal in scope to benefits provided under a typical employer plan and cover at least the following 10 categories: ambulatory patient services; emergency services; hospitalization; maternity and newborn care; mental health and substance use disorder services (including behavioral health treatment); prescription drugs; rehabilitative and habilitative services and devices; laboratory services; preventive and wellness services and chronic disease management; and pediatric services, including oral and vision care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan benefits must map to these categories; Secretary's EHB definition must reflect a typical employer plan's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Secretary's EHB definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1302(b)(4)(A)-(D) requires the Secretary to define EHB in a manner that: (1) reflects appropriate balance among the 10 categories; (2) is not designed to discriminate based on age, disability, or expected length of life; (3) takes into account the health care needs of diverse segments of the population; and (4) does not allow denials of EHB based on age, life expectancy, disability, degree of medical dependency, or quality of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EHB specification must consider nondiscrimination and population diversity; design choices should avoid systemic exclusion of subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catastrophic coverage eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1302(e) establishes that catastrophic coverage may only be offered to individuals who: (1) are under the age of 30 before the plan year; (2) have been certified as exempt from the individual responsibility requirement because coverage is unaffordable; or (3) have been certified as experiencing a hardship with respect to obtaining coverage under a QHP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catastrophic plan enrollment eligibility is statutorily limited; issuers must apply eligibility rules when offering catastrophic coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP certification criteria: provider choice and ECP inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1311(c) requires that QHPs ensure a sufficient choice of providers and include essential community providers (ECPs) that serve predominately low-income, medically-underserved individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Networks and provider selections are certification factors; ECP inclusion is a specific certification requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange procedures for certification/recertification/decertification
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1311(d)(4)(A) requires Exchanges to implement procedures for certification, recertification, and decertification of health plans as QHPs consistent with guidelines developed by the Secretary under section 1311(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges must have documented, Secretary-consistent procedures for plan lifecycle certification activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange authority to certify QHPs based on Secretary criteria and interests of enrollees
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1311(e)(1) grants an Exchange authority to certify a health plan as a QHP if the plan meets the Secretary's certification requirements and the Exchange determines making the plan available is in the interests of qualified individuals and employers in the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchange discretion operates within Secretary standards and consideration of state-specific enrollee/employer interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: State option to require benefits beyond EHB and State defray payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1311(d)(3)(B) permits a State to require QHPs to cover benefits in addition to EHB and requires the State to make payments (to enrollee or issuer) to defray costs of State-required benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States choosing to mandate additional benefits must fund or compensate for the added costs per statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single risk pool and optional merging of risk pools
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1312(c) generally requires an issuer to consider all enrollees in all health plans offered by such issuer to be members of a single risk pool for its individual and small group markets; States may opt to merge individual and small group market risk pools under section 1312(c)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk pooling rules affect issuer rate-setting and transfer calculations; State options can alter pooling structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for agents/brokers to enroll and assist with APTC/CSRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1312(e) authorizes the Secretary to establish procedures under which a State may allow agents or brokers to enroll qualified individuals and employers in QHPs offered through Exchanges and to assist individuals in applying for APTC and CSRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may set standards and procedures for agent/broker roles in enrollment and premium tax credit/cost-sharing reduction assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary oversight of Exchange financial integrity and operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1313 and 1321 provide the Secretary authority to oversee the financial integrity of State Exchanges, ensure compliance with HHS standards, reduce fraud and abuse, and allow State flexibility in operation and enforcement of Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS oversight may include measures deemed appropriate to protect program integrity while permitting State operational flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: User fee authority for Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: When operating an FFE, HHS has authority under sections 1321(c)(1) and 1311(d)(5)(A) to collect and spend user fees; OMB Circular A-25 Revised establishes federal policy on user fees, assessing charges for special benefits beyond those received by the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges may charge identifiable recipients for special benefits per federal policy; user fees must conform to OMB guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic Health Program (BHP) option and eligibility thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1331 provides States the option to establish a BHP to offer coverage for individuals under 65 with household incomes between 133% and 200% FPL (or effectively 138% in expansion States), providing benefits at least consisting of EHB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States operating BHPs must design eligibility and benefit parameters consistent with statute and minimum EHB content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment program purpose and Secretary's role
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1343 establishes a permanent risk adjustment program to transfer payments to issuers that attract higher-than-average risk enrollees, and directs the Secretary, in consultation with States, to establish criteria and methods for carrying out risk adjustment; Secretary operates the HHS program in States that fail to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk adjustment methodology, criteria, and methods are Secretary-defined; HHS can operate the program when States don't.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium stabilization programs composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Premium stabilization programs refer to the risk adjustment, risk corridors, and reinsurance programs established by the Affordable Care Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory actions and Payment Notices address design and parameters for these interrelated programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catastrophic plan regulatory definition and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A health plan is a catastrophic plan if it: (1) meets applicable individual market requirements; (2) does not offer coverage at the bronze/silver/gold/platinum levels; (3) does not provide coverage of EHB until the enrollee reaches the annual limitation in cost sharing; and (4) covers at least three primary care visits per year before reaching the deductible. Catastrophic plans may not impose cost-sharing for preventive services in section 2713.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catastrophic plan design must satisfy these discrete criteria to be treated as catastrophic under market rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate review program requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rate Review Rule (May 23, 2011) implemented a rate review program with subsequent amendments across multiple Federal Register notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers must comply with rate filing and review requirements as established in rate review regulations and subsequent amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange standards: network adequacy and ECP certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchange implementation included standards for eligibility, network adequacy, and essential community provider (ECP) certification standards (Exchange Establishment Rule and subsequent notices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network adequacy and ECP certification are enforceable Exchange criteria affecting QHP certification and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange user fee and standardized plan option policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment Notices set standards related to Exchange user fees and policies to implement standardized plan options, including limits on non-standardized plans and user fee adjustments for FFEs and SBE-FPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges and issuers must follow user fee rules and constraints on plan offerings intended to reduce choice overload and standardize consumer offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Enrollment Period (SEP) parameters and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations and Payment Notices have set and revised parameters for SEPs, established new SEPs for certain circumstances, lengthened SEP for those who lose Medicaid, and required all Exchanges to conduct SEP verifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEP eligibility windows and verification processes are Exchange operational standards; changes affect enrollment timing and verification burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider network requirement for Exchange-certified plans
rubrics_metrics.description: For the 2024 Payment Notice, finalized requirement that all plans seeking certification on the Exchanges utilize a provider network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QHPs on Exchanges must demonstrate an adequate provider network as part of certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on non-standardized plan options to reduce plan choice overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy finalized to reduce the risk of plan choice overload by limiting the number of non-standardized plan options that issuers may offer through Exchanges on the Federal platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers' ability to offer non-standardized options on the Federal platform is constrained to simplify consumer choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for dependent children and enrollment effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized rules lengthened SEPs for some populations and prohibited QHPs on FFEs and SBE-FPs from terminating coverage mid-year for dependent children who reach applicable maximum age; amended coverage effective date rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enrollments and continuity protections for dependents are regulated; effective date rules affect when coverage begins following enrollment or SEP events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange verification and assister solicitation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized policies on verifying consumer income and permitting door-to-door assisters to solicit consumers, and established consent and eligibility application documentation requirements for agents, brokers, and web-brokers assisting Exchange consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consumer verification processes and assister conduct/documentation are regulated to protect consumer information and enrollment integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness standard to resolve enrollment data inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 2026 Payment Notice, codified a timeliness standard for State Exchanges to review and resolve enrollment data inaccuracies at §155.400(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges must meet prescribed timelines for identifying and correcting enrollment data inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to deny QHP certification for failure to meet §155.1000 criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized at §155.1000 that an Exchange may deny certification to any plan that does not meet the criteria at §155.1000(c), and revisions to reconsideration standards at §155.1090 for FFEs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification denials are grounded in explicit regulatory criteria; issuers have reconsideration processes subject to revised standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public release of Exchange-submitted data
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized publicly releasing certain data and information that State Exchanges submit to HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State Exchanges should expect specified submissions to be publicly available per finalized policy; data governance and disclosure rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR loading permissibility conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmed that CSR loading practices permitted by State regulators are permissible under Federal law to the extent that they are actuarially justified and the issuer does not receive reimbursement for such CSR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CSR loading by issuers must be actuarially justified and not reimbursed to be permissible under federal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single final version of Actuarial Value (AV) Calculator
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized that HHS will only release a single, final version of the AV Calculator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers and Exchanges must use the final AV Calculator version designated by HHS for AV calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized plan option AV and differentiation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Updated standardized plan option designs for PY 2026 to ensure AVs are within the permissible de minimis range for each metal level and amended §156.201 to require issuers to meaningfully differentiate standardized plan options from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized plans must meet AV tolerances and be meaningfully distinct to avoid consumer confusion and preserve metal level integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-conducted ECP certification reviews in States doing plan management
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized that HHS would conduct ECP certification reviews in States performing plan management functions beginning PY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS oversight includes ECP certification review authority where States perform plan management activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-RADV methodological changes: Super HCCs and error rate adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted creation and application of Super HCCs in the sorting step that assigns HCCs to failure rate groups; finalized a sliding scale adjustment in HHS-RADV error rate calculation; added a constraint for negative error rate outliers; and transitioned from prospective application of HHS-RADV adjustments to applying results to risk scores from the same benefit year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit/validation methodology for risk adjustment data validation (HHS-RADV) has specific sorting and error-rate rules issuers and auditors must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-RADV sampling and IVA/SVA changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning with benefit year changes, excluded enrollees without HCCs from the IVA sample; removed the Finite Population Correction (FPC) from IVA sampling methodology; replaced Neyman allocation data source with most recent 3 consecutive years of HHS-RADV data; modified SVA pairwise means test and increased initial SVA subsample size; changed materiality thresholds for random and targeted sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling and statistical methodology for HHS-RADV audits have been revised; issuers and auditors must align to new sampling rules and thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) requirement for audit observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized that in certain cases, HHS may require a corrective action plan to address an observation identified in an HHS risk adjustment program audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audited entities may be required to implement CAPs when audits identify deficiencies or observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Payment Pre-Testing and Assessment (IPPTA) for Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Implemented IPPTA requirements for State Exchanges to ensure adherence to the Payment Integrity Information Act of 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exchanges must perform pre-testing and assessments related to improper payments per IPPTA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and documentation for agents, brokers, web-brokers, and DE entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalized consent and eligibility application documentation requirements for agents, brokers, and web-brokers assisting Exchange consumers; applied certain standards to web-brokers and Direct Enrollment entities across all Exchanges; and addressed authority to investigate and undertake compliance reviews/enforcement at the insurance agency level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party assister entities must meet documentation, consent, and conduct standards; HHS has authority to suspend or enforce against agents/agencies for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustments to transfer reduction requests and State reduction authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted a State flexibility framework permitting States to request a reduction in HHS risk adjustment State transfers, with later repeal of the ability for some States to request reductions beginning with 2024 benefit year (and approvals of specific percentage reductions for Alabama in certain years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State transfer reduction requests have been permitted historically but later constrained; States and issuers must follow prevailing transfer reduction policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications responding to legislative changes (WFTC provisions affecting PTC/APTC)
rubrics_metrics.description: WFTC legislative provisions amend 26 U.S.C. 36B and related rules to change PTC/APTC eligibility (e.g., PTC allowed only for 'eligible alien' for plan years beginning 2027; elimination of PTC eligibility for some lawfully present individuals under certain conditions; changes to coverage month definitions and APTC repayment limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuers, Exchanges, and tax filers must account for statutory eligibility changes affecting premium tax credits and reconciliations in plan years/tax years specified by WFTC.
